haas_alarms.title: SERVO ERROR TOO LARGE
haas_alarms.description: The axis position following error exceeded the maximum allowed value. The motor cannot keep up with the commanded position.
possible_causes: Mechanical binding or obstruction on the axis
Worn or damaged ballscrew, linear guides, or bearings
Excessive feed rate or acceleration settings
solutions: Power off and check for mechanical binding — move axis by hand
Inspect ballscrew, linear guides, wipers, and bearings
Reduce rapid override to 25% and test — if alarm clears, check parameters
Check servo drive LEDs for secondary fault codes
Check Parameters 15 and 16 (following error limits)
Verify correct lubrication on all axes

haas_alarms.title: SERVO DRIVE FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The servo amplifier/drive has detected an internal fault condition.
possible_causes: Short circuit in motor or cables
solutions: Power cycle the machine and monitor if alarm returns
Check servo drive LEDs for specific fault code
Inspect motor cables for damage or shorts
Verify cabinet cooling fans are operational
Check incoming power voltage and stability

haas_alarms.title: AXIS NOT HOMED
haas_alarms.description: A program or function was requested that requires the machine to be homed first.
possible_causes: Machine was powered on but axes were not homed
E-Stop or alarm occurred during homing
solutions: Press POWER/RESTART, then press ZERO RET to home all axes
If home switch fault, check Parameters 22 and 1 for home direction/offset
Verify home switch signals in Diagnostics > Inputs

haas_alarms.title: AXIS MOTOR OVERLOAD
haas_alarms.description: The axis motor current draw exceeded the overload limit. Thermal or current overload protection activated.
possible_causes: Worn ballscrew or bearings requiring more force
Crash or tool contact with fixture
solutions: Power off and check for mechanical obstruction on the affected axis
Lubricate ballscrews and linear guides
Allow machine to cool for 30 minutes before restarting
Check for loose motor coupling
Inspect and replace worn ballscrew/bearings if needed

haas_alarms.title: DRIVE OVER TEMPERATURE
haas_alarms.description: A servo amplifier reached its thermal limit. The drive will shut down to prevent damage.
possible_causes: Drive has been overloaded for extended period
solutions: Allow machine to cool — wait 30–60 minutes before restart
Check all cabinet cooling fans are spinning correctly
Clean dust from drive heat sinks and cabinet vents
Verify ambient temperature is within specification (< 40°C)
Reduce duty cycle or cutting loads

haas_alarms.title: SERVO DRIVE DISCONNECT
haas_alarms.description: Communication between the CNC and servo drive was lost.
possible_causes: Loose or damaged servo drive communication cable
Power supply issue to the drive
solutions: Check servo drive cable connections at both the drive and the MOCON/IOPCB
Power cycle the machine fully (main breaker off, wait 30s, on)
Inspect cables for pinching or damage

haas_alarms.title: HARD LIMIT — POSITIVE DIRECTION
haas_alarms.description: An axis reached its positive hard travel limit switch.
possible_causes: Program error causing axis to exceed travel boundary
solutions: Jog axis away from limit switch in negative direction
Check work offset coordinates — tool may be positioned outside workpiece area
Verify G-code coordinates are within machine travel limits
Check limit switch input signal in Diagnostics

haas_alarms.title: HARD LIMIT — NEGATIVE DIRECTION
haas_alarms.description: An axis reached its negative hard travel limit switch.
possible_causes: Program error causing axis to travel past negative boundary
solutions: Jog axis away from limit switch in positive direction
Verify work offsets and tool length offsets are set correctly
Check G-code for incorrect negative coordinate values

haas_alarms.title: TOOL OFFSET NOT SET
haas_alarms.description: A G43 tool length compensation call references an H offset that is zero or not set.
possible_causes: Tool not measured or manually entered
Wrong H number in G43 command
solutions: Measure the tool with the tool setter and enter length in offset table
Verify the H number matches the tool offset entry number
Use G43 H[tool_number] matching your tool setup

haas_alarms.title: SOFT LIMIT — POSITIVE DIRECTION
haas_alarms.description: The programmed move would exceed the positive software travel limit.
possible_causes: Incorrect work offset placed near edge of travel
Tool length offset not applied, causing Z overtravel
solutions: Verify work offset (G54) is correctly set — it may be too close to machine limits
Check all axis coordinates in the program relative to machine travel
Ensure tool length offset is loaded (G43 H_) before Z moves
Review soft limit Parameters (43–48)

haas_alarms.title: SOFT LIMIT — NEGATIVE DIRECTION
haas_alarms.description: The programmed move would exceed the negative software travel limit.
possible_causes: Program has excessive negative Z depth
solutions: Check Z work offset — if set at zero instead of actual surface, all Z moves will be too deep
Verify tool length offset is active (G43 H_)
Reduce depth-of-cut values in program

haas_alarms.title: E-STOP — EMERGENCY STOP
haas_alarms.description: Emergency stop was activated. All motion has been halted.
possible_causes: Safety door was opened during a cycle
Servo fault triggered the E-STOP chain
solutions: Investigate and resolve the cause of the E-STOP before resetting
Twist the E-STOP button clockwise to release it
Press RESET to clear the alarm
Check for other active alarms that may have caused the E-STOP
Check safety door interlock switch if door-related

haas_alarms.title: TOOL NUMBER TOO LARGE
haas_alarms.description: The T number in the program exceeds the number of pockets in the tool changer.
possible_causes: Program written for a machine with more pockets
Incorrect T number typed in program
Machine parameter for tool count is set incorrectly
solutions: Check T number in program — it must not exceed the number of available pockets
Verify machine tool capacity in Parameter 65
Update program with valid tool numbers

haas_alarms.title: NO TOOL IN SPINDLE
haas_alarms.description: An M06 tool change was commanded but the spindle does not contain the expected tool.
possible_causes: Tool was manually removed from spindle
Previous tool change did not complete correctly
ATC carousel is out of sync
solutions: Manually insert the correct tool into the spindle
Use ATC recovery to synchronize the carousel
Check ATC pocket sensors and verify tool presence detection

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE NOT ORIENTED
haas_alarms.description: The spindle did not reach its orientation position before tool change.
possible_causes: Heavy tool causing spindle to coast too far
solutions: Check spindle encoder signal in Diagnostics
Verify orient speed Parameter (Parameters 257, 258)
Check spindle brake operation
Power cycle and retry — orient failure can be intermittent

haas_alarms.title: MISSING FEEDRATE
haas_alarms.description: A cutting motion (G01, G02, G03) was commanded without an active feedrate (F word).
possible_causes: F word missing from the program block
Modal feedrate was cleared without being reset
solutions: Add an F word to the first cutting move: G01 X_ Y_ F100.
Verify F value is non-zero
Check that G94 (feed per minute) or G95 (feed per rev) is active as expected

haas_alarms.title: DIVIDE BY ZERO
haas_alarms.description: A program calculation resulted in division by zero.
possible_causes: Macro variable used as divisor is zero or uninitialized
Formula in G-code macro has zero denominator
solutions: Review custom macro code for division operations
Add a check: IF [#VAR NE 0] before dividing
Initialize all macro variables to safe values at program start

haas_alarms.title: SUBPROGRAM NOT FOUND
haas_alarms.description: An M98 call references a subprogram that cannot be found in memory or on the device.
possible_causes: Subprogram was not loaded to the machine
Incorrect P number in M98 call
solutions: Load the subprogram to the machine memory
Verify P number in M98 matches the actual program number O_ of the subprogram
Check if subprogram is on USB or NetShare — machine may not be searching there

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE LOAD MONITOR
haas_alarms.description: Spindle load exceeded the programmed threshold. This is a warning alarm — cycle may have been halted.
possible_causes: Feed rate too high for material and tool
solutions: Inspect and replace the cutting tool
Reduce feed rate and/or depth of cut
Check Material Override and Tool Load Monitor settings
Verify spindle load limit Parameter (setting 84)

haas_alarms.title: DOOR OPEN DURING CYCLE
haas_alarms.description: The machine door interlock detected the door is open while a cycle is running.
possible_causes: Safety door opened by operator during cycle
Door latch or interlock switch malfunction
solutions: Close the safety door completely and press CYCLE START
Check door latch mechanism for proper engagement
Test door switch signal in Diagnostics > Inputs
Do NOT bypass the interlock — safety hazard

haas_alarms.title: PARAMETER OUT OF RANGE
haas_alarms.description: A parameter value entered is outside the allowed range for that parameter.
possible_causes: Manual parameter entry with invalid value
solutions: Identify which parameter triggered the alarm (noted on screen)
Check Haas documentation for valid range of that parameter
Enter a valid value within the specified range

haas_alarms.title: HOME SWITCH NOT FOUND
haas_alarms.description: The home switch was not detected during the homing (zero return) sequence.
possible_causes: Axis moved past the switch location
solutions: Check home switch wiring connections at both the switch and the I/O board
Test home switch signal in Diagnostics > Inputs
Verify Parameter 1 (zero return direction) is set correctly
Manually trigger the switch with a screwdriver to test

haas_alarms.title: ATC ARM FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The automatic tool changer arm encountered a fault during tool change.
possible_causes: Heavy or oversized tool jammed the ATC
Tool not fully seated in pocket
solutions: Do NOT force the ATC manually — follow the ATC recovery procedure
Press ZERO RET to run ATC recovery sequence
Check air pressure supply (minimum 90 PSI / 6.2 bar)
Inspect ATC arm sensor signals in Diagnostics
Ensure all tools are properly seated and within weight limits

haas_alarms.title: LOW LUBE FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The automatic lubrication system is low on lubricant or has a fault.
solutions: Check the lube reservoir level and refill with recommended way oil (ISO VG 32)
Prime the lube pump manually using the purge button
Inspect lube lines for kinks or blockages
Check the lube pump output pressure
Do not run machine long without lubrication — causes guide and screw damage

haas_alarms.title: LOW MEMORY
haas_alarms.description: The program memory is nearly full. New programs cannot be loaded.
possible_causes: Many large programs stored in memory
solutions: Back up programs to USB or network share
Delete programs that are no longer needed
Use the DNC (direct numerical control) mode for large programs instead of loading to memory

haas_alarms.title: LOW BATTERY
haas_alarms.description: The backup battery for memory retention is low and needs replacement.
possible_causes: Battery at end of life (typically 3–5 years)
solutions: Replace the 3.6V lithium backup battery as soon as possible
Do NOT power off the machine until battery is replaced — memory could be lost
After replacement, verify parameters and offsets are still intact
Part number: Haas 32-0261 (or equivalent 3.6V 1/2AA lithium)

haas_alarms.title: AXIS DRIVER OVERTEMPERATURE
haas_alarms.description: A servo amplifier (axis driver) is overheating. The drive will derate or shut down.
possible_causes: Cabinet cooling fans failed or blocked
Excessive cutting load for extended period
Drive heat sink fins clogged with dust
solutions: Allow machine to cool 30–60 minutes before restarting
Clean all cabinet cooling fans and heat sink fins
Verify all fans are running in the electrical cabinet
Check room ambient temperature — max 40°C (104°F)
Reduce aggressive cutting cycles

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE DRIVE FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The spindle drive (VFD/inverter) has detected an internal fault.
possible_causes: Spindle motor overload or short circuit
Input power fault (voltage drop or phase loss)
solutions: Power cycle the machine completely (main breaker off, wait 30s)
Check spindle drive display for fault code — document and look up in Haas service manual
Verify three-phase power supply is balanced and within spec
Check spindle motor winding resistance
Ensure spindle brake is released before running

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE OVERLOAD
haas_alarms.description: The spindle motor load exceeded the overload threshold.
possible_causes: Feed rate or depth of cut too aggressive
solutions: Inspect and replace cutting tool
Reduce feed rate using feed override
Reduce depth of cut or step-over
Improve chip evacuation with coolant and air blast
Check spindle load limit setting (Setting 84)

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE SPEED ERROR
haas_alarms.description: The spindle could not reach or maintain the commanded speed within the allowed time.
possible_causes: Spindle load too high — stalled or near stall
Encoder fault — spindle speed feedback incorrect
solutions: Reduce programmed spindle speed and load
Check spindle encoder signal and wiring
Inspect belt condition and tension (if belt-drive model)
Check spindle drive for fault codes

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE ORIENT FAILURE
haas_alarms.description: The spindle failed to reach the orient position for tool change within the timeout period.
possible_causes: Orient speed or timeout parameter set incorrectly
Spindle encoder or position sensor fault
Heavy tool assembly with high inertia
solutions: Check Parameters 257 and 258 (orient speed and direction)
Increase orient timeout Parameter if using heavy tooling
Verify spindle encoder signal
Test spindle brake engagement

haas_alarms.title: ATC FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The automatic tool changer has encountered a general fault condition.
possible_causes: Tool changer arm or carousel is jammed
Tool not latched in carousel pocket
solutions: Follow the Haas ATC Recovery Procedure (see programming manual)
Check air pressure supply (must be ≥ 90 PSI / 6.2 bar)
Inspect ATC carousel for jammed tools or debris
Check all ATC sensor inputs in Diagnostics
Do not manually force the ATC mechanism

haas_alarms.title: TOOL POSITION ERROR
haas_alarms.description: The ATC carousel is not in the expected position or a tool was not found in the expected pocket.
possible_causes: ATC carousel lost position (power interruption during tool change)
solutions: Run ATC recovery: press ZERO RET or use the ATC FWD/REV keys carefully
Verify all tools are in their programmed T positions
Use ATC > CAROUSEL to manually position and verify pocket locations
Check carousel home sensor signal

haas_alarms.title: TOOL LIFE EXCEEDED
haas_alarms.description: Tool Life Management indicates the tool has reached its programmed usage limit.
possible_causes: Tool has been used for the full programmed life (time or cycles)
Tool Life Management feature is active and has flagged the tool
solutions: Replace the tool in the ATC pocket with a fresh tool
Reset tool life counter for that tool number
Review and adjust tool life limits if they are too conservative or too aggressive

sinumerik_alarms.title: Following error too large
sinumerik_alarms.description: The position following error (difference between command and actual position) of an axis exceeded the maximum tolerance.
possible_causes: Mechanical binding, friction, or axis obstruction
Drive enable signal missing or drive fault
solutions: Check for mechanical obstruction — move axis by hand (machine off)
Verify the drive enable signal is active in PLC I/O
Check the KV (servo gain) parameters using Siemens startup tools
Inspect lubrication of guides and ballscrews
Check for additional drive alarms (380xxx series)

sinumerik_alarms.title: Contour monitoring: velocity too high
sinumerik_alarms.description: The actual axis velocity exceeded the contour monitoring tolerance band.
solutions: Emergency stop the machine
Check encoder wiring and polarity
Verify drive enable chain is correct
Check for additional drive alarms

sinumerik_alarms.title: Controller enable missing
sinumerik_alarms.description: The hardware enable signal for axis control is not present. Axis movement is not possible.
possible_causes: PLC has not released the axis enable (DB21 bit not set)
solutions: Check and reset the Emergency Stop
Close all safety doors and reset interlocks
Check PLC ladder for axis enable logic (DB21)
Verify safety relay output signal

sinumerik_alarms.title: Program not found
sinumerik_alarms.description: The NC program or subprogram called could not be found in the part program memory.
possible_causes: Program not transferred to the CNC memory
solutions: Transfer the required program to the NC memory via USB or network
Verify the program name matches exactly (case-sensitive on some versions)
Check the program search path in the machine data
Use the program manager to confirm the program exists in the correct directory

sinumerik_alarms.title: Feedrate = 0
sinumerik_alarms.description: A feed-dependent motion command was executed but the active feedrate is zero.
possible_causes: F word missing from the program block
G63 (tapping mode) active without correct feedrate
solutions: Add F value to the motion block: G1 X_ Y_ F100
Check feed override potentiometer is not at 0%
Verify the correct feed group is active (G93/G94/G95)

sinumerik_alarms.title: Spindle speed exceeds maximum
sinumerik_alarms.description: The programmed spindle speed exceeds the machine or gear stage maximum.
possible_causes: S value too high for current gear stage
Machine data for maximum speed set too low
solutions: Reduce the S (spindle speed) value in the program
Select the correct gear range (M40/M41/M42/M43)
Verify maximum speed limits in machine data MD35100

sinumerik_alarms.title: Tool not found in tool management
sinumerik_alarms.description: The tool number called (T word) is not defined in the tool management system.
possible_causes: Tool not created in tool management
Tool was deleted from tool management
solutions: Create the tool in the tool management with correct number and type
Verify T number in program matches the tool management database
Check if tool was accidentally deleted and re-enter geometry data

sinumerik_alarms.title: Program end not found — M30/M02 missing
sinumerik_alarms.description: The NC controller reached the end of the program file without finding an M30, M02, or RET.
possible_causes: M30 or M02 missing at end of main program
Wrong file loaded (a subprogram loaded as main program)
solutions: Add M30 at the end of the main program
Verify the correct program file was transferred completely
Check that the program is a main program and not a subroutine

sinumerik_alarms.title: Subprogram nesting depth exceeded
sinumerik_alarms.description: The maximum subprogram call depth (typically 8 levels) has been exceeded.
possible_causes: Recursive subprogram call (program calls itself directly or indirectly)
Too many levels of subroutine nesting
solutions: Restructure program to reduce nesting depth
Check for accidental recursive calls (subprogram calls itself)
Reduce number of nested CALL/MCALL levels

sinumerik_alarms.title: Axis move commanded while spindle stopped
sinumerik_alarms.description: A feed move was commanded while the spindle was not rotating. This is blocked as a safety measure.
possible_causes: M3 or M4 not programmed before feed moves
solutions: Ensure M03 S_ (or M04 S_) is programmed before any G01/G02/G03 moves
Check that the spindle has actually reached speed (use M3/M4 with SPOS or dwell G4)
Verify spindle enable signal in PLC diagnostics

sinumerik_alarms.title: Axis cannot be referenced (homed)
sinumerik_alarms.description: The homing sequence for the axis could not be completed successfully.
possible_causes: Reference switch not found or signal missing
Axis at or past the reference switch already
solutions: Check reference switch wiring and signal in PLC diagnostics
Jog axis away from reference position and retry
Verify encoder cable and connector
Check machine data for reference point parameters (MD34000–MD34100)

sinumerik_alarms.title: Axis must be homed (referenced) first
sinumerik_alarms.description: An operation requiring a homed axis was requested but the axis has not completed its reference point approach.
possible_causes: Machine was just powered on and axes not homed
An alarm cleared the homed status
solutions: Perform reference point approach: activate REF mode and press axis + key
Home all axes in correct sequence as specified by machine builder
Check for alarms that may have reset the homed status

sinumerik_alarms.title: Emergency stop activated
sinumerik_alarms.description: The Emergency Stop button has been pressed or the E-STOP chain has been interrupted.
solutions: Identify and resolve the cause of the E-STOP before clearing
Release the E-STOP button (twist clockwise)
Press RESET on the operator panel
Check the PLC diagnostics for the E-STOP chain signal
Check all safety door and light curtain statuses

sinumerik_alarms.title: No valid tool for spindle
sinumerik_alarms.description: No usable tool was found in the tool management for the requested T function.
possible_causes: Tool life expired and no sister tool defined
Tool geometry data incomplete or invalid
solutions: Check tool management — verify tool status is active (not expired/blocked)
Enter or correct tool geometry data (length, radius, type)
Define a sister tool if tool life management is active
Reset tool life counter if tool was replaced

sinumerik_alarms.title: Tool not present in magazine
sinumerik_alarms.description: The requested tool is defined in tool management but not physically present in the magazine.
possible_causes: Tool management and physical magazine are out of sync
solutions: Physically verify the tool is in its assigned magazine pocket
Check magazine pocket sensor for the affected position
Use tool management to update tool location or reassign pocket
Synchronize tool management data with physical magazine state

sinumerik_alarms.title: Feedrate limitation active
sinumerik_alarms.description: The programmed feedrate was clamped by a machine-data limit. Actual feedrate may be lower than programmed.
possible_causes: Programmed feedrate exceeds axis maximum velocity (MD32000)
Rapid traverse override is active at reduced rate
solutions: Check feed override and rapid override percentages
Verify programmed F value is within axis capabilities
Review machine data MD32000 (maximum axis velocity)

sinumerik_alarms.title: PLC: NC not ready
sinumerik_alarms.description: The PLC is indicating that the NC (numerical control) is not in a ready state.
possible_causes: Communication fault between NCK and PLC
solutions: Check NC status and clear any active alarms
Power cycle the control — allow full boot sequence to complete
Check NCK hardware for fault indicators (LEDs)
Contact machine builder or Siemens service if issue persists

sinumerik_alarms.title: Drive: motor overtemperature warning
sinumerik_alarms.description: The motor temperature sensor reports the motor is approaching or has exceeded its thermal limit.
solutions: Allow machine to cool — reduce cycle duty or take a break
Check motor cooling fan is spinning
Verify ambient temperature is within spec (max 40°C)
Reduce cutting load (feed, depth of cut, or speed)
Check motor thermistor wiring at motor connector

sinumerik_alarms.title: Drive: overcurrent / short circuit
sinumerik_alarms.description: The drive detected an overcurrent condition in the power stage or motor winding.
possible_causes: Motor winding short circuit or insulation breakdown
solutions: Check motor insulation resistance with a megohmmeter (should be > 1 MΩ)
Inspect motor cable for damage, chafing, or pinching
Measure motor winding resistance — all phases should be balanced
If motor and cables are good, suspect the drive power module

sinumerik_alarms.title: Drive: encoder fault
sinumerik_alarms.description: The position encoder feedback signal is missing, incorrect, or has a hardware fault.
possible_causes: Encoder cable damaged, disconnected, or with a loose connector
Wrong encoder type configured in machine data
solutions: Check encoder cable connections at both the motor and the drive module
Inspect cable for damage, especially at cable entry points
Measure encoder supply voltage (typically 5V or 24V depending on type)
Verify machine data for encoder type matches installed hardware (MD30200–MD30250)
Replace encoder if all wiring checks out

sinumerik_alarms.title: PLC: Emergency stop activated
sinumerik_alarms.description: The PLC has activated the emergency stop condition. All drives have been disabled.
possible_causes: Safety circuit open (door, guard, light curtain)
PLC program error triggering E-STOP output
solutions: Check and release E-STOP button (twist to release)
Verify all safety doors are closed and guards are in place
Check PLC diagnostics for the specific input that triggered the E-STOP
Press RESET after clearing the cause

sinumerik_alarms.title: PLC: Feed hold active
sinumerik_alarms.description: The PLC feed hold signal is active. Axis motion and spindle operation are inhibited.
possible_causes: Feed hold button pressed on operator panel
PLC interlock condition active (e.g., coolant door, workpiece clamp)
External signal holding the feed hold input
solutions: Check if the feed hold button on the operator panel is engaged
Review PLC diagnostics for which interlock is asserting feed hold
Ensure workpiece clamping, coolant doors, and other interlocks are satisfied
